title: Thousands of flights canceled as airlines work to dig out from nationwide ground stop
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Airlines canceled thousands of flights across the U.S. on Saturday as they worked to recover from a nationwide ground stop a day earlier that left passengers scrambling for seats and disrupted travel around the world.
The U.S. air travel schedule should be back to normal by the end of Sunday, two days after what was the nation’s longest ground stop in 25 years, Bryan Bedford, administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, said. He said airlines “will still have delays and cancellations” Saturday but promised that the “worst is behind us.”
New technology being added to the nation’s air traffic control system overloaded antiquated equipment and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to Friday’s ground stop that lasted more than four hours, Trump administration officials said.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told reporters Saturday that a contractor had been replacing a section of the system’s old copper wire with new fiber wire, and that work somehow caused the system overload. Duffy said officials were investigating whether contractor “incompetence” or a faulty router was the cause.
“Our contractor didn’t meet the moment,” Duffy said, blaming L3Harris Technologies Inc.
Andrew Charlton, an aviation consultant, said Friday’s stoppage affected about a quarter of the 45,000 flights in the U.S. each day.
“The knock-on effect of that is incredible,” said Charlton, managing director of Aviation Advocacy. “The aircraft doesn’t just fly from A to B and back to B and then stop. It then moves onto C and then over to E and around and around and around. It is, of course, exacerbated if you’re talking about long-haul flights, international flights over the Atlantic or over the Pacific.”
Thousands of flights delayed and canceled
At airports across the U.S. on Saturday, passengers were still scrambling to figure out how to get to their destinations.
Dan Russell, 66, learned his connecting flight from Kona, Hawaii, to Fresno, California, was canceled a half-hour before boarding was scheduled in San Diego on Friday night. San Diego hotels were full, so he and his wife waited at the airport for a rebooked flight on Saturday.
“There’s nothing you can do,” he said, as his wife, Mary, tried to nap on his shoulder.
In Las Vegas, Korean Mexican influencer Sujin Kim, known online as Chingu Amiga, said her Friday flight to Mexico was rescheduled for Saturday morning. Kim said she had never experienced anything like it, though she travels often and “I always lose my suitcase.”
“Many people ended up sleeping at the airport, too, but thank God we managed to find a room,” she said.
Sports teams scheduled to play this weekend adjusted game start times after rescheduling flights and chartering buses. No. 19 Mississippi’s game at Oklahoma was delayed a full day to Sunday.
FlightAware, a website that tracks flights, said more than 4,100 flights had been canceled Saturday. Cirium, a similar site, put that number above 3,200 flights.
Officials say no one was in danger during ground stop
Duffy reiterated Saturday that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights in the air at the time of the grounding order landed safely.
Trump administration officials also continued to blame Congress for failing to approve more funding to replace the decades-old technology that helps manage the U.S. air traffic. Duffy said that 70% of the system had been replaced with fiber optic wire but that his agency also needs new air traffic control towers and runways.
In a moment that perhaps only further underscored the Transportation Department’s struggling systems, Duffy’s news conference Saturday morning began with audio troubles that forced last-minute microphone swaps.
Charlton, the aviation consultant, said the problem was due to updating a system that can never shut down.
“What you’re watching here is trying to change the tires of your car when the car’s going at 80 miles an hour down the expressway, because nothing stops in aviation,” Charlton said. “It’s a 24/7 operation. And to make changes on the fly, if you’ll pardon that pun, is incredibly complex and dangerous.”
Past problems have been linked to equipment failures
The problem appeared similar to a regional air traffic control communication outage in September that snarled hundreds of flights across the Northeast, although that disruption was linked to a construction crew cutting a fiber optic line. Aging equipment was also blamed for brief radar outages last year that disrupted Newark airport.
Aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said the difference this time was the nationwide scale of the disruption, which left controllers unable to reliably talk to pilots.
It differed from the one after 9/11 because planes were not being told to land immediately and pilots likely were able to communicate with ground controllers at airports, Arroyo said.
___
This version has been updated to correct that Duffy said investigators were looking at whether a possible faulty router, not a faulty wire, might have been the cause
___
Kruesi reported from Providence, Rhode Island. Associated Press journalists Josh Funk in Omaha, Nebraska, Elliot Spagat in San Diego, Bernice Bautista in Las Vegas, and Hannah Fingerhut in Des Moines, Iowa, also contributed.

title: Port of New Orleans sues tanker owners following ship collision on Mississippi River
text:
NEW ORLEANS (WVUE/Gray News) - The Port of New Orleans has filed a $1 million federal lawsuit against the owners of the tanker vessel that struck and sank a New Orleans riverboat on Friday.
The lawsuit was filed Friday evening in the Eastern District of Louisiana and names the Atlantic Asphalt MV, Nave Shipping SA, and Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd. as defendants.
It alleges the maritime mishap caused at least $1 million in damage to the Thalia Street Terminal where the paddlewheel cruise ship American Heritage was docked.
An arrest warrant was also issued, directing federal marshals to seize and hold the marine vessel Atlantic Asphalt, a 525-foot ship that on Friday afternoon appeared to lose control as it passed beneath the Crescent City Connection bridge, according to court documents.
The tanker veered to the right, striking the docked river cruise ship American Heritage, causing it to capsize and partially sink.
The riverboat had 192 passengers aboard, but authorities said all were rescued safely, with 32 requiring hospital treatment.
“As a result of the Atlantic Asphalt’s allision with the American Heritage and the incident, the Board’s Thalia Street Terminal was significantly damaged,” the lawsuit noted. “The extent of said damage remains under investigation, but physical damage is currently estimated to exceed $1 million with additional substantial direct, indirect and consequential damages anticipated.”
The lawsuit identifies Nave Shipping SA as a corporation registered in the country of Liberia.
“According to publicly available information, Nave Shipping is the registered owner and ship manager and commercial manager of the Atlantic Asphalt,” the suit said.
Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd. is identified in the suit as a private limited company based in Singapore.
According to the lawsuit, Thome is the Atlantic Asphalt’s ISM manager, “responsible for the effective implementation of the ‘International Safety Management’ code aboard the tanker.
The lawsuit said the Port of New Orleans board has “incurred and will continue to incur additional damages and expenses including ... cleanup, surveys, repair, replacement and salvage costs, resulting in a maritime lien against the Atlantic Asphalt.”
The claim cites “negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness of the Atlantic Asphalt” as the cause of the allision, a term referring to a moving vessel striking one that is securely moored.
“As a result, ... the Atlantic Asphalt, Nave Shipping, Thome (and potentially other parties not yet identified with responsibility for the operation, condition, crewing and seaworthiness of the Atlantic Asphalt) are solidarily liable for all damages sustained by The Board,” the lawsuit said.
Plaintiffs in the lawsuit listed are the Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans, represented by attorneys Christopher Hannan, Sara Kuebel, and Abigail Weiland of the high-powered New Orleans law firm Jones Walker.
Court records show the initial case assignment allotted to federal magistrate Karen Wells Roby and to U.S. District Judge Wendy Vitter, chief judge at the federal courthouse in New Orleans.

title: Richard Sterban, member of the celebrated country and gospel group The Oak Ridge Boys, dies at 83
text:
Richard Sterban, the bass vocalist of the Grammy-award winning gospel quartet The Oak Ridge Boys and a country music hall of famer, died Saturday, his family and the band said in a statement. He was 83.
Sterban, who had been with the band since 1972, died in Hendersonville, Tennessee, due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after a long battle with cancer, they said.
Sterban left his job as a backup singer for Elvis Presley to join the vocal group, which perhaps became best known for its rendition of “Elvira.” Sterban toured regularly with the group until 2025, when his health deteriorated.
The Oak Ridge Boys won five Grammy awards and were nominated 23 times. They performed for presidents, on American Bandstand, at the Grammy Awards ceremony and at the Grand Ole Opry. They toured with Johnny Cash and sang backup vocals on Paul Simon’s hit “Slip Slidin’ Away.”
Sterban and the band’s three other members were inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015, joining Presley. They joined the Vocal Group Hall of Fame in 2001. And in 2011 they gained membership in the Grand Ole Opry.
A native of Camden, New Jersey, Sterban was inducted into the Philadelphia Music Hall of Fame in 1994 along with Joe Bonsall, another Oak Ridge Boys member who died in 2024 and who sang with Sterban in the Keystones.
In a statement, Country Music Hall of Fame CEO Kyle Young said Sterban “used his unmistakable bass voice to connect commercial country music to its deep gospel roots” and called him a “steady force and a foundational figure in country music.”
“He helped the supergroup achieve seventeen No. 1 hits, legions of fans the world over, and a well-deserved place in the Country Music Hall of Fame,” Young said.
The band’s golden period in the ’80s and beyond included 1981’s “Elvira,” the 1982 hit “Bobbie Sue” and 1983’s “American Made.” “Elvira” was a massive crossover moment for the group, reaching No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on Billboard’s all-genre Hot 100.
Sterban is survived by his wife, Donna; daughters Lauren and Tori; sons Rich, Doug and Chris; and 11 grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

title: Bruins trounced by Wild
text:
BOSTON — Ryan Hartman and Danila Yurov scored two goals each, Jesper Wallstedt stopped 29 shots, and the Minnesota Wild beat the Boston Bruins 6-2 on Saturday night to extend their road winning streak to eight games.
Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak to 11 games (six goals, 14 assists) with two assists for the West-leading Wild, who have earned at least a point in 11 straight games (9-0-2).
Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman scored 67 seconds apart in the opening two minutes of the second period for Minnesota, which cruised to its NHL-best 10th road victory. Yurov scored both of his in the third period, the second an empty-netter.
David Pastrnak and Fraser Minten scored for Boston, which lost its second straight home game after winning seven in a row at TD Garden. Both losses came wearing their new mostly brown “varsity jerseys” with bright yellow numbers, trim and helmets that they debuted Thursday.
After getting pulled in Boston’s lopsided loss Thursday against Montreal, Jeremy Swayman started and made 19 saves.
Hartman’s first came on a wrister from the left circle that beat Swayman inside the far post, making it 1-0 at 6:54 of the opening period.
Hughes slipped a wrister past Swayman 53 seconds into the middle period,and Coleman’s slap shot from the point found its way past a few bodies and into the net, making it 3-0.
Minten’s power-play goal came at 8:45, but Hartman’s second just 75 seconds later took away Boston’s brief momentum.
The Wild won the first meeting of the season, 4-1, at home on Oct. 3 when Kaprizov scored two goals.
The teams entered tied with the NHL’s second-best goal differential, plus-24, behind only Carolina.
Up Next
Wild: Host Nashville on Tuesday night
Bruins: Close their four-game homestand on Tuesday, facing Los Angeles

title: Historic homecoming for a Bangor soldier killed at Pearl Harbor, almost 85 years later
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Nearly 85 years after he was killed at Pearl Harbor, a Bangor soldier made a historic homecoming.
Family and community members gathered at Brookings-Smith Funeral Home on Saturday morning to remember Pfc. Willard C. Orr, the only Bangor resident to die in the Dec. 7, 1941, attack. He was 21 years old.
Orr’s nephew, Thomas Orr, said his family knew him by his middle name, Carleton. During the ceremony, he spoke of his uncle’s military service and shared passed-down family memories of him.
“He enlisted in the United States Army Air Corps in December 1940. He was assigned to Mitchell Field in Long Island, and then was transferred to Hickam Field in Hawaii in March 1941,” Orr described of his uncle during the service. “Following the attack on Pearl Harbor, Carleton was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart.”
For decades, Orr’s family waited for answers about their missing loved one. Thomas Orr said the Army contacted the family about five years ago to collect DNA samples.
“It took several years. Late last year, early this year, they notified us to say they had a confirmed match and wanted to return his remains from Hawaii to Maine,” explained Orr. “It’s a sad day, in a way, remembering his death, but also a time for celebration for bringing him home after 85 years.”
After the service, a procession made its way to Maple Grove Cemetery, where Orr will be laid to rest in the family plot.
For Orr’s great-nephew, Timothy Sargent, the homecoming was a chance to honor a family member he learned about only after joining the military.
“I hadn’t actually known until it was after I joined the military, I’ve been in for about 24 years now or so,” Sargent recalled. “It was a couple of years after I joined that my grandfather just casually mentioned in passing that he had a brother that died at Pearl Harbor, I was like, ‘That’s a pretty big deal!’ So, it was a pretty big shock.”
Family members traveled from as far away as Indianapolis to attend Saturday’s service. After years without answers, Orr’s return offers them a chance for closure.
“Unfortunately, my grandfather, everything was open-ended for them. They never got any remains. They never got anything. Just a missing in action letter and some of his medals,” Sargent detailed. “So, it is really good that we were able to, even after that much time had passed, not forget about it and remember the sacrifice and the honor that we can pay to them now.”
In 2021, the city honored Orr’s memory with the Willard C. Orr Pedestrian Bridge in downtown Bangor.

title: Tufts women’s soccer eliminates Husson in NCAA Tournament
text:
As a freshman at Tufts University in 2023, Emily Nicholas scored two goals as the Jumbos tied Husson University 2-2 in Bangor.
Now a senior, Nicholas again scored against Husson and it proved to be the game-winner as the seventh-ranked Jumbos beat the Eagles 2-0 in the first round of the NCAA Division III women’s soccer tournament at Vassar College in Poughkeepsie, NY on Saturday.
Nicholas converted a pass from the right wing by fellow All-NESCAC first team selection Waverly Sumner just 7:19 into the game.
It was her seventh goal of the season.
Audrey Cromett sewed up the win by scoring her third of the season with 11:53 remaining in regulation.
Tufts, now 14-1-3, will play Vassar on Sunday in the second round.
Husson finished up at 10-6-2.
Gigi Edwards made two saves in posting her sixth shutout of the season and 27th of her career. Biddeford’s Gabriella Smith made seven stops for Husson.
Tufts had a 22-4 edge in shot attempts and a 9-2 advantage in shots on goal.
Olivia Charles and Sanford’s Hailey Tarbox had Husson’s shots on goal.
The Jumbos also had a 12-3 edge in corner kicks.

title: 17-year-old surfer saves person who jumped from Golden Gate Bridge
text:
SAN FRANCISCO (KGO) - It was a dramatic rescue in the shadow of the Golden Gate Bridge.
A group of surfers helped save a person who jumped from the bridge Tuesday afternoon, reaching him before a U.S. Coast Guard boat arrived.
Voices coming from the top of the Golden Gate Bridge alerted a group of surfers that something was wrong.
“I yelled to my dad, like, call someone. Everyone was yelling to the beach to call someone. And then he ended up just jumping off,” 17-year-old Colby Ralls said. “There were guys up there, like, telling him not to, and he just jumped off. And just right as we saw that happen, me and a couple of other guys that were out there just started paddling to go get him.”
Ralls of San Rafael was in the water with two other surfers and knew they had just seconds to get to him.
“He was yelling, ‘Help,’ as we were paddling towards him. You know, he’s still alive,” Ralls said.
The three strangers grabbed the man they believe was in his 20s.
“We’re all kind of just helping, like stabilizing the board and just keeping him afloat because he couldn’t really swim. And, you know, the guys were talking to him like, ‘hey, it’s OK. It’s OK. We’re getting help,’” Ralls said.
Within minutes, a Coast Guard rescue boat made it to them.
“They’re going fast. You know, they’re like, ‘We need to go. We need to go. We need to,’ because it was just such a miracle that he even survived that drop. You know, it’s kind of crazy,” Ralls said.
U.S. Coast Guard Lieutenant John Thompson was part of the watch team Tuesday afternoon.
“Hitting that water at that speed, and you can experience shock very quickly. So those surfers being there, to be able to pull the person onto a surfboard, provided those vital seconds in order to be able to save the person,” Thompson said.
Ralls and the two other surfers went back to shore, still processing what happened.
“I think people … there should be easier ways to get help for people like that, you know. I just, I just really hope he’s OK,” Ralls said.
The U.S. Coast Guard said the man was in stable condition when he was transferred to an ambulance.

title: Jaden Lipinski goal lifts UMaine hockey to win at Vermont
text:
University of Maine sophomore center Jaden Lipinski broke a 1-1 tie with a wraparound goal 2:29 into the third period and graduate student left wing and captain Owen Fowler scored on an empty net as the Black Bears upended Hockey East leader Vermont 3-1 at the Gutterson Fieldhouse on Saturday night.
UMaine extended its unbeaten streak to three games (2-0-1) while ending Vermont’s five-game stretch (3-0-2).
UMaine is now 6-5-1 overall and 2-3-1 in Hockey East while Vermont slipped to 5-4-2 and 4-2-2, respectively.
It is the eighth time this season UMaine has held an opponent to two goals or less and 10th in regulation as Holy Cross and Boston University scored in overtime to beat the Black Bears 3-2.
Freshman defenseman Dante Siciliano opened the scoring with his first career goal just 5:08 into the game but the Catamounts tied it just 1:03 later when junior right wing Ethan Burroughs tallied a power play goal.
It was Burroughs’ fourth of the campaign.
The score remained 1-1 until early in the third period.
Dru Krebs fired a diagonal pass from the right point to the left corner behind the net and it hit the open Lipinski in the chest.
Lipinski controlled the puck, wheeled around the net to the left of UVM goaltender Jacob Oster and swept a backhander from the edge of the crease that appeared to hit the stick of the goalie and roll behind him.
“I knew [Krebs] was going to find me back door. It came off his stick weird. It came off my chest and I was patient with it and saw a lane to the back post on the other side,” the 6-foot-4, 210-pound Lipinski said. “That’s what we’ve been working on, especially us big guys. It was nice to execute it.”
There was a brief delay before the referee gave the “goal” signal.
“I didn’t really know what happened. If you just get it there, good things will happen,” Lipinski said. “My focus was just to get it in the paint and, obviously, when I found out it went in, it was pretty exciting.”
It was Lipinski’s second goal of the season and fifth of his career and four of them have been game-winners.
The Catamounts pulled Oster in favor of the extra attacker late in the game and Fowler scored into the empty net with 13 seconds remaining.
Jeremy Langlois and Lee Parks assisted on Fowler’s third of the season.
Siciliano opened the scoring when he skated from the point to between the faceoff circles unattended and took a pass from Tanner Klimpke and wristed the puck past the glove side of Oster.
Burroughs tied it when he found himself all alone in front of Albin Boija, took a long pass from Cedrick Guindon and flipped a backhander past the stick side of Boija.
Boija finished with 22 saves and Oster wound up with 25 stops.
UMaine protected the lead well in the third period, outshooting the Catamounts 10-6.
“That’s a testament to our conditioning and how hard we work,” Lipinski said.
UMaine coach Ben Barr was pleased with the win.
“We had a good push there on the road against a good team and that’s not easy,” Barr said. “It’s good to see us find another level in the third period.
UMaine regained the services of junior defenseman and Ohio State transfer Chris Romaine, who missed the last seven games with an upper body injury.
He led the UMaine defense in shots on goal with three.
“He looked good. He was very steady, he didn’t panic. He played hard. It was good to have him back,” Barr said.
UMaine will entertain Boston College on Friday and Saturday night at 7 while Vermont will visit UMass Lowell for a two-game set.

title: Son of former CIA Director John Brennan arrested on child sexual abuse images charge
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The son of former CIA Director John Brennan was arrested Friday on a federal charge related to child sexual abuse images, according to authorities.
The case against Kyle Owen Brennan brought in federal court in Virginia stems from an investigation by local authorities that was referred to the FBI earlier this year, according to court papers.
An attorney for Kyle Brennan did not immediately return a phone call seeking comment.
Local authorities began investigating after the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children received a tip in 2024 about suspected child sexual abuse material uploaded to his Adobe account, according to an affidavit filed in court.
His cellphone was seized that year as part of the local investigation before the case was referred to the FBI in October, the court papers say. An FBI review of data from the phone uncovered child sexual abuse images, according to the affidavit.
John Brennan, who served as CIA director under President Barack Obama, has been under scrutiny by President Donald Trump’s Justice Department over allegations that he lied to Congress during 2023 testimony.
John Brennan has vigorously denied those allegations, which relate to the intelligence community assessment that Russia had launched an influence campaign during the 2016 U.S. presidential election with a goal of boosting the Republican over Democratic opponent Hillary Clinton.
Prosecutors have not filed charges despite warning his lawyers that he is a target of their probe. Brennan has also been entangled in a broader conspiracy investigation in Florida scrutinizing Trump adversaries, but that inquiry has shown signs of floundering.

title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting, White House says
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet Thursday on the sidelines of next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China’s tech hub of Shenzhen — an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.
While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs and say they will be heavier in symbolism than substance.
Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed by the White House on Friday and the Kremlin on Saturday. It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries.
Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers.
Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.
The U.S. president has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the U.S. war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles.
Trump does plan on discussing the Iran war with Xi and Putin, but will steer away from discussing Ukraine, according to a senior U.S. official who briefed reporters on the condition of anonymity.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
The trilateral meeting is intended to serve as the “beginning of hopefully a conversation” on nuclear disarmament “that can be productive going forward,” said the U.S. official, who added that no agreements are expected to be announced.
But Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.
Trump administration officials acknowledge that the nuclear stockpile issue is a difficult one for Beijing to engage on, but the U.S. official characterized the meeting as the moment for China to “step up ... to the adult table” on a matter of international importance.
Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit
By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China’s growing clout and prestige.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signaling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they’re making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don’t like,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.
More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China’s argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia’s war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.
The trilateral meeting could undercut China’s push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism,” he said.
The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years
Putin and Xi are no strangers. They’ve fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.”
Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the No. 1 trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.
As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia’s energy resources and became Moscow’s principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.
In the lead-up to Russia’s war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship.” China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv’s Western allies played a part in provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine.
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing’s policy on issues related to Taiwan.
Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.
Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which the leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalized plans for establishing the United Nations.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can’t be enforced on others.
“It’s clear that a meeting between the leaders of countries such as Russia, China and the United States is extremely significant,” Peskov said. “However, let’s not forget that the vision for a global order is that no one tries to impose any particular view of global order, and it should be based entirely on mutual benefit and mutual respect.”
___
Wu reported from Bangkok and Isachenkov from Moscow.

title: When will flights be back to normal after nationwide ground stop?
text:
When will flights be back to normal after nationwide ground stop?
Some flights had resumed as of Saturday morning, but many passengers remained stranded.
When will flights be back to normal after nationwide ground stop?
Some flights had resumed as of Saturday morning, but many passengers remained stranded.
Stranded travelers were still trying to get home on Saturday morning after the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years snarled air travel, affecting thousands of flights.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday that operations were slowly returning to normal after the Federal Aviation Administration lifted the ground stop on Friday night. He said it is safe to fly.
At a press conference on Saturday, Bryan Bedford, the head of the Federal Aviation Administration, said the worst is behind us, but estimated that there would still be around 5,000 flight cancellations as airline crews are repositioned.
"That will set us up for full recovery tomorrow," Bedford said.
Why was there a ground stop?
The Trump administration said the pause was ordered out of an abundance of caution and no lives were at risk.
Officials blamed "intermittent" communications and radar gaps for the disruption. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system appeared to overwhelm older parts of the system.
Duffy offered new details on Saturday. He said the system overload seemed to stem from "routine maintenance" in a remote location on Friday, as contractors were upgrading an outdated telecommunications line. He said it wasn't clear whether the issue was caused by contractor error or faulty equipment.
Duffy once again urged Congress to fully fund efforts to modernize antiquated air traffic control infrastructure.
"If we don't make these upgrades, we have a less safe system. We can't continue on technology of the 80s," Duffy said
Duffy said there's no indication that a cyberattack or foreign interference caused the issue. He said there is "zero chance" that it was caused by the rollout of a new AI-powered system called SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories), comments echoed by the company that designed the system on social media.
What can stranded passengers do?
If your flight gets cancelled, airlines owe you a full cash refund if you choose not to rebook, according to Brian Kelly, the founder of The Points Guy.
"Do not let them give you a voucher. By law, they have to give you a refund if you choose not to take the flight they try to re-accommodate you on," Kelly said.
The bad news for travelers is that airlines aren't required to pay you back for additional travel expenses in this case.
"This would not be what's considered a controllable cancellation, meaning it's not the airline's fault, and so in the vast majority of cases, people would not get reimbursed for hotel expenses, rental cars, food vouchers, parking fees, or any other kinds of expenses. It doesn't hurt to ask," said Teresa Murray, consumer watchdog director for the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG).
Kelly said travel insurance should pay for those costs, while others may be eligible for relief through certain travel credit cards with trip delay and cancellation coverage.
"Some credit card companies will exclude FAA mass shutdowns and some won't," Kelly said. "My best tip: keep all your receipts, submit them to your credit card company, let them decide. Don't try to read the policy...and hope for the best."

title: FBI part of investigation into credible bomb threat at Illinois ethanol plant
text:
PEORIA, Ill. (WEEK/Gray News) - The mass evacuation of neighborhoods within a one-mile radius of an Illinois ethanol plant continued Saturday after police said a suspicious package was determined to be a credible bomb threat.
While the package found at BioUrja Renewables was “rendered safe,” Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said a search was being conducted at the South Peoria plant.
Search of the facility continues
Dixon said the company notified police of the threat at 1:08 p.m. He said bomb technicians rendered the package safe just over seven hours later.
At a news conference at 12:40 a.m. Saturday, Dixon asked for the public’s patience as investigators search the large facility for other explosive devices.
Ryan Presley, special agent in charge of the FBI’s Springfield office, declined to provide additional details. He said investigators will work “tirelessly” to find whoever is responsible and “bring them to justice.”
Mayor confirms device
About two hours earlier, Peoria Mayor Rita Ali addressed reporters at Manual Academy on South Griswold Street, which was being used as an evacuation shelter.
“A device has been identified. We know it’s a credible threat. We know it’s a bomb,” Ali said.
She was the first to confirm a bomb was found.
“We don’t know if there are other devices,” Ali said.
Evacuation order and shelters
The evacuation order went into effect at 7:02 p.m. Peoria police released a statement saying the department was investigating a reported bomb threat at BioUrja Renewables, formerly the ADM plant, at 1 Edmund Street.
The statement urged anyone who lives or works within a one-mile radius of the facility to evacuate homes and businesses until further notice.
Police asked people to avoid the one-mile area around the facility until further notice. The statement said most streets in the area have been closed.
According to the statement, officers were on scene conducting an investigation and search of the facility to determine the credibility of the threat and ensure public safety.
Dixon said early Saturday that about 70 people were housed in the shelter at Manual. City officials said EastSide Centre is the designated shelter for East Peoria.
Late Friday night, East Peoria’s government reported the evacuations would remain in effect. Another update on the evacuations will come no later than 9 a.m. Saturday. Peoria police planned another briefing at noon Saturday.
Employers respond
Caterpillar told employees not to report for third shift Friday night.
“Due to guidance from local officials on the safety situation in downtown Peoria, employees should not report for third shift. Please follow local law enforcement guidance on this developing situation,” the company said.
OSF HealthCare St. Francis Medical Center, downtown Peoria’s largest employer, released a statement saying it was taking “all appropriate precautions.”
“The safety and well-being of our patients, visitors and Mission Partners remain our top priority. We are taking all appropriate precautions in response to the situation in downtown Peoria and are working closely with local authorities. We will continue to monitor the situation and take any additional steps necessary to maintain a safe environment for those we serve and those who work at our facilities,” the hospital said.
OSF Life Flight also released a statement saying its emergency medical helicopters and their radio communications have not been affected.
“It is not business as usual tonight, it is business as trained. Emergency medical helicopters and their radio communications have not been affected, and we will continue to provide only safe transportation. We always have a policy that ensures everyone arrives safely, and will continue offering support to our hospitals, agencies and other partners as needed,” OSF Life Flight said.

title: Yarmouth football rolls to 8-man Large title
text:
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
AUBURN — The Yarmouth High football team has had one of the most dynamic offenses in the state all season.
On Saturday, the Clippers rode that offense to a state championship.
Senior quarterback Iggy McGrath and junior running back Stephen Connolly had big games to lead Yarmouth to a 72-26 win over Old Town in the 8-man Large School final at Edward Little High School.
Yarmouth capped an 11-0 season with its second 8-man title, and fourth state championship overall.
McGrath completed 15 of 18 passes for 371 yards and six touchdowns, while Connolly ran for 166 yards and four touchdowns on 16 carries. The Clippers, who were averaging 62 points per game entering the state final, had 559 total yards.
“It feels unbelievable,” said Connolly. “We’ve been working hard for this all year, and it means more than anything. We wanted this so bad, worked hard every week, and we got it done.”
Old Town finished with a 9-2 record. Charlie Degrasse led Old Town’s offense with 111 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Quarterback Ethan Closson ran for 51 yards and a touchdown and also had 207 yards in kickoff returns, with two touchdowns.
Yarmouth led just 6-0 after the first quarter but pulled away quickly in the second. The Clippers scored on each of their offensive possessions in the second quarter, highlighted by a 55-yard strike from McGrath to Jackson Jabar, and led 38-12 af the half.
McGrath credited good play-action fakes with Connolly that allowed receivers to get separation down field.
“Most of the (scoring plays) came off play-action, which stems from a great fake (handoff) with Stephen,” McGrath said. “He obviously carries a lot of the eyes on the defense. He’s the No. 1 threat. He’s an insane running back. The (defense) has to bite on the run just to try and stop him, and I’ve just got Jackson Jabar open (from there).”
Yarmouth kept its momentum going in the second half, scoring on each of its drives until the backups took over late in the fourth quarter. Jabar finished with five receptions for 180 yards and two touchdowns. Flanagan had four catches for 111 yards and three touchdowns.
“It really was a super team,” Yarmouth coach Nick Orsi said. “We’d love to say it’s the coaching, but when you have the best running back, the best QB, the best receiver … We had a great line and skill guys.”
The Clippers were stout on defense as well. Yarmouth’s defensive line put pressure on Closson all afternoon. Freshman defensive back Hudson Clark had two interceptions, including a 38-yard return for a touchdown.
Before this year, Yarmouth last won a Gold Ball in 2022 — a 30-24 victory over Waterville for the 8-man Large crown. The Clippers also won two 11-man titles in Class C (2010 and 2011).

title: Flagg, Mavericks lose to short-handed Cavaliers
text:
CLEVELAND — Tyrese Proctor posted his first triple-double with 24 points, 11 rebounds and a career-best 10 assists in leading the short-handed Cleveland Cavaliers to a 127-117 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday night.
Australia native Proctor became the first Cleveland player with a triple-double since Max Strus against Charlotte on April 14, 2024. The points and assists were career-highs for Proctor, and he also matched his pro high in rebounds.
The Cavaliers played without their usual starting lineup, as Donovan Mitchell (left knee), James Harden (left calf), Evan Mobley (left big toe), Jarrett Allen (right knee) and Peyton Watson (right hamstring) were sidelined because of injuries. Sixth man Sam Merrill (right hamstring) also was inactive. The Cavs ruled out all of their starters after travel delays following the nationwide ground stop on Friday and having to stay overnight in South Florida after a loss to the Miami Heat.
Former Cleveland guard Kyrie Irving scored 20 of his 34 points in the third quarter for Dallas, while Cooper Flagg had 18 points and eight rebounds. Flagg hugged fellow 2025 draftee — and former college teammate — Proctor shortly after he earned his 10th assist on a pass to Mario Hezonja.
Proctor buried back-to-back 3-pointers in the fourth to give Cleveland the largest lead of the evening at 113-91. Irving drained a long 3-pointer with 2:23 left to pull the Mavericks within 122-112, but then missed a 31-footer on their next possession that could have brought them within seven.
Irving, who made the go-ahead 3-pointer in winning Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals for the Cavaliers, received the loudest ovation of any player when introduced.
Hezonja scored 22 points, rookie Meleek Thomas had a season-high 20, and Norchad Omier scored his first 13 NBA points and grabbed eight rebounds off the bench for Cleveland.

Mavericks: At Boston on Sunday
Cavaliers: Host Chicago on Monday

title: NH man killed in early-morning crash on I-95 in Saco

title: Students return to class for first time since deadly Oregon school shooting
text:
BEND Ore. (KPTV/Gray News) - While cars and buses still moved through the drop-off lines, Justinna Rosett said most Silver Rail parents took a different approach to the start of school Thursday.
“Everybody walked their kids. Everybody talked to one another. The sense of community was really nice,” she said.
It was the first day back for families since a shooting last month at the Bend school left three students and a teacher dead.
“It was pretty hard for me as a mom,” parent Nicole Ybarrondo said. “I mean, I held it together to the best of my ability.”
Rosett said she felt mixed emotions. She has a fourth-grader.
“He wants to go back,” she said. “Kids are so resilient. I think it affects me more than him, to be honest.”
Leaders of Bend-La Pine Schools said going back to school is the best thing for most students. However, everyone needs to return in their own way and at their own speed.
“Returning to routine and predictable schedules and experiences are really good for kids as they navigate this trauma,” said Karen Rush, executive director of elementary schools.
Rush said they tried to make the day feel as normal as possible while still acknowledging the tragedy and offering support to those who needed it.
To help with the transition, Thursday was an early release day. Teachers started off by reading grade-appropriate scripts to their class about what happened.
There were counselors on site for all students and staff who needed extra support, as well as a new school resource officer who came out of retirement to work at Silver Rail full-time.
“I’m really grateful that we have one,” Rosett said. “I feel for all the schools that don’t.”
The district also replaced damaged doors and locks, added privacy screens to certain windows, and blocked off the area where the shooting happened.
Before coming back officially, parents had the chance to bring their kids for a walk-through. Ybarrondo said it was tougher than expected.
“I don’t think I was even prepared for my daughter’s reaction,” she said. “It turned into a trauma tour of sorts. ‘Mom, let me show you where I was running to find a place to hide. Let me show you the closet that I hid in. Let me show you where I was when it started.’”
The district said more than 90% of the students came back to school Thursday. The rest may have requested transfers to other schools within the district. Others might have withdrawn entirely and are now homeschooling or exploring other options.

title: Orono football rallies past Old Orchard Beach to win 8-man Small School title
text:
Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
AUBURN — The Orono football team managed just one yard in the first half of the eight-man Small School title game against Old Orchard Beach on Saturday.
The Red Riots recovered in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter, to win their second eight-man state championship with a 22-14 victory over the Seagulls at Edward Little High School.
“(The first half) was bad, very bad,” said Orono quarterback Cooper Brown, who was 5 of 13 passing for 154 yards and two touchdowns. “But we knew what we were capable of, and we knew the game wasn’t over yet.”
Brown also ran four times for 54 yards and a score for Orono (6-4), which has won 13 state championships overall. The Red Riots also won the eight-man Small title in 2023 when they beat Old Orchard Beach 46-18.
The game was tied 14-14 with about two minutes to play when Brown dropped back to pass. He scrambled to his right and darted down the sideline for a 49-yard touchdown run. He then hit Ritchie Watson for the 2-point conversion to give the Red Riots a 22-14 lead.
Old Orchard Beach returned the ensuing kickoff to the Orono 32. A pass from Charron to tight end Scout Schilling moved the Seagulls to the 5, but Schilling fumbled and it was recovered by Orono linebacker Josh Wood with 1:28 left.
Orono took a knee on three consecutive plays before deciding to punt with 20 seconds remaining. Brown, serving as punter, hit Watson, the upback, with the kick, and it was recovered by Charron at Orono’s 4-yard line, giving the Seagulls one more opportunity.
Charron threw three straight incompletions, including a toss that bounced off the hands of Schilling in the end zone. On fourth down, Charron tried running to his right, only to be met by Wood and Eli Schaff for a loss, sealing Orono’s victory.
“We’ve been battle-tested all year,” said Schaff, who had three receptions for 85 yards. “We knew what we could do out there. We were just like, ‘Let’s go.'”
After their stagnant first half, the Red Riots moved the ball better in the third quarter but still trailed 14-0 heading into the fourth.
They scored their first touchdown with 9:10 left in the contest. Watson took a toss from Brown, moved to his right, and promptly threw the ball back to a wide open Brown, who had a clear path to the end zone for a 20-yard touchdown.
“I’m not the (main) target (on the play),” Brown said. “I knew they were going to run to Ritchie, they had been running to Ritchie all night. I told him, ‘Look my way, I’ll be open.'”
Orono tied the game on the next drive when Brown hit Dylan Forbes, who had a step on Evan Moody, for a 48-yard scoring strike.
Orono started the season 0-3, including a 30-22 loss at Old Orchard Beach on Sept. 11, before winning six of its final seven games.
“This team, I’ll tell you, the adversity they’ve been through all year long (was intense),” said Orono coach Bob Sinclair, whose son, Tyler Sinclair, returned home Friday after successful heart surgery to repair a torn aorta and blood clot. “We start 0-3. Then my son has an issue with his aorta. Our kids have welcomed him into their hearts, he does filming for us, he does middle school (football) for us. This will be a group of kids I’ll never forget.”
Old Orchard Beach finishes 10-1. Sophomore running back Brayden Koelker led the Seagulls with 157 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Junior quarterback Matthew Charron had 79 yards on 18 carries.
Old Orchard Beach was playing in its fifth straight state title, with wins in 2024 and 2022.

title: Scam selling tickets to a fake Noah Kahan event now disabled
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Scam selling tickets to a fake Noah Kahan event now disabled
A scam listing selling tickets to a fake Noah Kahan event in Freeport has now been disabled.
The fake event was posted to the ticketing website Eventbrite and was promoted as an evening concert with singer-songwriter Noah Kahan set for June 12, 2027 at the L.L Bean Flagship store.
Jason Sultham, Manager of Public Affairs at L.L Bean told Maine's Total Coverage that the store has no affiliation with the listing and that "no such event ever existed."
He adds that once the scam was discovered, L.L. Bean immediately notified Eventbrite and disabled the listing.
Tickets for Noah Kahan's, now sold out, "The Last of The Bugs World Tour" went on sale on Thursday. Since then, many fans took to social media advising that scammers were trying to sell fake tickets to those who couldn't secure any.
The "Sticks Season" singer will kickstart his "The Last of The Bugs World Tour" April 24, 2027 at Sanford Stadium in Athens, Georgia.
Kahan will also be performing for six nights at Fenway Park in Boston, MA with opening acts Buffalo Traffic Jam and Tiny Habits.

title: New Orleans port sues to get control of tanker that crashed into cruise ship on Mississippi River
text:
New Orleans port sues to get control of tanker that crashed into cruise ship on Mississippi River
The Port of New Orleans has filed a federal lawsuit against the tanker that struck a river cruise ship Friday.
Court records show the Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans filed the lawsuit against the Atlantic Asphalt, Nave Shipping, and Thome Ship Management. It lists a $1 million demand in the maritime property damage case.
Court records also show the Port asked for a warrant. A federal judge granted that request, and the warrant was issued. No word right now on if it has been served.
Related video above: Drone 6: Aerial footage shows massive response to rescue operation after cruise ship struck in New Orleans
According to the lawsuit, the tanker struck the American Heritage cruise ship Friday afternoon, as passengers were getting off the ship. The port accuses the tanker and the companies responsible for it of failing to follow safety protocols. The port is seeking money to cover cleanup, inspections, repairs, and any other expenses related to the crash.
The tanker has been towed away from the site, but it could take weeks to move the cruise ship, which remains turned on its side against a terminal in the Mississippi River, Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham told reporters Saturday.
The first step is to make sure the 16,000 gallons (60,500 liters) of fuel on the boat are removed safely, she said.
Traffic has been limited on the Mississippi River, but Burnham said boats should be able to move both upstream and downstream soon.
The tanker appeared to lose steering, but the exact cause of the crash is not known, Burnham said. The National Transportation Safety Board was sending investigators to New Orleans.
All 197 passengers and crew on the American Heritage cruise ship survived Friday as well as the crew on the tanker.
Officials said 32 people were brought to the hospital, including two police officers thrown into the Mississippi River when the boat rolled. But none of the injuries were critical and eight remained hospitalized Saturday.
The National Transportation Safety Board said the tanker’s voyage data recorder has been recovered. A 16-member team will spend a week in New Orleans investigating the incident.
NTSB member John DeLeeuw said the agency expects to release a preliminary report within 24 to 30 days, with the final investigation report expected in 18 to 24 months.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: A quiet night, some snow showers tomorrow, then a calm week
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - A few snow showers may stick around for some of the far western reaches as well as the north but they won’t amount to much accumulation if anything into tomorrow. Otherwise it will be a generally quiet and cool weekend for most. Highs will be in the 40s with lows in the 20s and mostly cloudy skies across the board. Next week will also start off quite quiet as well with very little precipitation in the foreseeable future.
Tonight: Cold with light winds
A mainly cloudy night across the region with chilly lows falling into the upper to middle 20s generally. Winds will remain quite light.
Sunday: Another round of light snow showers possible out west, otherwise cloudy
Another round of light snow showers may come through western reaches of the state but once again they will not accumulate at all pretty much. A few places may see a dusting on cold surfaces but those areas will be few and far between. Everyone will just see a mostly cloudy sky with a NW breeze at 10-15 mph.
Sunday night: Very similar to Saturday night
Almost a copy of the previous night with temps dropping into the middle to upper 20s for most under a mainly cloudy sky and light winds.
Monday and beyond: Another quiet week ahead
High pressure dominates the pattern once again and we don’t really see any chances for precip over the next week or so here in Maine. The rather quiet pattern we have been in will continue with pretty seasonable temperatures expected.
Sunday: Mainly cloudy with a few snow showers west. Highs in the 30s and 40s. Winds light.
Sunday night: An overcast night mostly. Lows in the 20s. Light winds
Monday: Some clearing and warmer temps. Highs in the 50s and light winds.

title: Memorial opens honoring victims of the 2015 Charleston church massacre
text:
It took Alana Grant years to find the strength to set foot in the basement of Mother Emanuel AME Church in Charleston, where her grandfather, the Rev. Daniel Lee Simmons, attended his final Bible study.
Her fears have been replaced by gratitude and hope now that there is a completed memorial in a courtyard by the front door for the “Emanuel Nine,” the Black churchgoers killed by an avowed white supremacist in 2015.
The memorial provides a public space where “people can go and remember really what happened here,” Alana Grant said as she and her husband, state Rep. Hamilton Grant, got their first look.
On Saturday, the long-planned memorial at the South’s oldest African Methodist Episcopal Church opens to the public.
Emphasizing remembrance and reflection, the marble memorial is anchored by a Fountain of Grace, symbolizing God’s eternal love and mercy. Water flows from a shallow basin etched with the names of the six women and three men slain. Two Fellowship Benches with curved backs, sheltering anyone seated, flank the fountain. There is also a Cross of Hope, signifying redemption in the wake of suffering. A garden honoring the five survivors will come next.
The Rev. Eric Manning, co-chair of the Mother Emanuel Memorial Foundation board, hopes it will mean something to everyone.
“I was actually standing out there the other day,” said Manning, who took over after pastor and state Sen. Clementa Pinckney was among those killed. “Just for a moment, a peace came over me.”
How the memorial is helping victims’ families
Grant sees the memorial as a place to inspire conversations with her three small children about their great-grandfather. Because the facts of the shooting have been so public, she doesn’t want them to hear more from someone else.
“I spent a lot of time thinking about it and praying about it,” she said. “I do want them to go so that they can kind of see what even brought me to South Carolina.”
Former North Carolina state senator and Charlotte City Councilman Malcolm Graham, whose sister Cynthia Graham Hurd died huddled under a desk in the fellowship hall, attended the 2023 groundbreaking. He has anticipated visiting the memorial to reflect on “all the good times Cindy and I had as kids growing up, and being at the church and going to Sunday school.”
A library, scholarship and other awards now carry the name of the accomplished librarian. Now she’ll live on in the memorial, too.
“She said before she died that I was the most famous person in the family,” Graham said. “She is the most famous person in our family and I still look up to her.”
As for the survivors to be honored with a garden, Grant says their living with memories of the shooting is “nothing short of heroism.”
“There are not a lot of spaces where you get to see the survivors. We as Black people have survived so much,” Grant said.
A church memorial that can be something for everyone
When a committee sought an architect in 2017, they heard from designers all over the world, said John Darby, another memorial foundation co-chair who runs a Charleston real estate development firm. The final candidates were not asked to submit design proposals, but instead give written responses to deep questions on topics like forgiveness.
That unconventional request was very prescient, said Michael Arad, an architect on the 9/11 Memorial whose design was ultimately chosen. He wrote about his admiration for the victims’ families who offered forgiveness to the shooter.
A white, Jewish New Yorker who had never visited South Carolina, Arad did a deep-dive into the community for more than a year after he was selected. Having lengthy conversations with members of the congregation and researching the church’s 200-year history was essential, he said, and while the 9/11 memorial was a bigger endeavor, this design wasn’t any less complex.
“My job as a designer was to allow people who visit the site to see and hear what was here all along,” he said. “We understand who we are as Americans through stories like this, through our response.”
Arad said he embraces emotionally weighted projects as “a tremendous privilege” and he “could not imagine turning down a project like this.”
The foundation has raised around $25 million over the last decade for the memorial, garden and other costs, much of it from foundations, endowments and corporations, Darby said.
“It was one of those things that people wanted to be a part of,” Darby said. “We don’t want it to be an expense to the church.”
Memorial stirs hope to learn from hate and tragedy
Established in 1818, Mother Emanuel was built by free and enslaved people. In the 20th century, the church became a place of resistance where the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. and other civil rights figures spoke.
The Emanuel Nine’s families applauded in 2015 when Gov. Nikki Haley removed the Confederate battle flag from state buildings. But with Republicans stirring an angry backlash against diversity and equity efforts, Graham said “racism, hatred and discrimination continue to be this country’s Achilles’ heel.”
Alana Grant has tried over the years to gather support for a hate crimes statute, and her husband is among the lawmakers who pushed legislation named for Pinckney that would add enhanced penalties for hate crimes to South Carolina’s criminal code. It failed to pass, even though a senator was among the Emanuel Nine.
She sees this memorial as an opportunity to raise “generational awareness” so younger people will campaign against hate. Tourists still come to the church daily out of curiosity or sympathy, and could leave the memorial feeling inspired.
“We want more than your thoughts and prayers. We want your advocacy,” she said.

title: Bucksport man arrested after wrong-way driving on I-95
text:
ARGYLE TOWNSHIP, Maine (WABI) - A Bucksport man was arrested after driving the wrong way on Interstate 95 early Saturday.

title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
text:
CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.
It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch, still the goal for accelerating moon and Mars travel.
Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.
The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster’s messy miss. Cameras panned the spacecraft up and down as it hung high above the ground, supported by the arms of the launch tower.
“Can you believe it?” SpaceX commentator Dan Huot shouted, dragging out each word. “Look at her! Baby, she’s back!”
Soon afterward, Musk congratulated his “incredible team.” SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, crucial for rapid and low-cost recycling. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.
NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars.
“It was almost magic,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said via X. “Making more believers by the day … one step closer to (emojis of the moon and the U.S. flag).”
The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-meter) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.
Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometers) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps.
It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit.
SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.
As for the booster, SpaceX’s Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down. The booster’s guidance system sensed it wasn’t in the right position and automatically initiated the watery detour and self-destruction. Engineers are still investigating the cause.
SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months. That is the starting point for NASA’s next Artemis mission, which will skip the moon and remain in orbit around Earth for lunar lander practice.
Artemis III’s four astronauts will attempt to dock their capsule with not only Starship but Blue Origin’s Blue Moon. The two companies will take turns delivering crews to the lunar surface. NASA is targeting as soon as 2028 for Artemis IV, humanity’s first moon landing since the Apollo era more than half a century ago.

title: Family of high school freshman who died after collapsing in class remembers ‘a good kid’
text:
EAGLE RIVER, Alaska (KTUU/Gray News) - Friends and family are remembering the life of an Alaska high school freshman who died from cardiac arrest after suddenly collapsing while playing football in physical education class last week.
Mary and James Curry said their son Levi was born with a heart condition, but had surgery to alleviate it.
“The surgery basically healed it,” James Curry said. “Other than that, he’s just like a normal kid.”
Youth football career
Those who knew Levi best agreed that he was seemingly born to play football, standing 6 feet 3 inches tall at just 15 years old.
“I think 17 years now, and I’ve never had a ninth grader start for varsity, especially on the offensive line,” Eagle River High School football coach Jonathan Wetzel said.
Curry’s family said Levi was named one of the best defensive players in the state on Wednesday.
“I called the coach and he told him, and Levi was so excited about that,” Mary Curry said. “He was really joyful and he called his dad to tell him.”
“I was out of town,” James Curry said. “That was the last conversation I had with him, and it was a good one.”
Remembered for kindness
More than a football player, Levi is remembered by those closest to him for his kindness and positive attitude.
“So many people have come up and shared their positive experiences with Levi, and now it’s proven that he’s just a good kid in general,” James Curry said.
“There was plenty of times that I could be having a bad day at work, and I could get to the ball field and you see him coming up, and his smile would just kind of wash that bad day away,” Wetzel said.
Funeral and community support
Levi’s funeral was held on Wednesday. Nearly 500 people attended to pay their respects and show support for the family.
“It’s just overwhelming, how much he meant to the community or what kind of impact he had,” Mary Curry said.
Levi had several siblings.
“It’s just amazing how many people just showed up for Levi,” Noah, Levi’s older brother, said.
“I wasn’t really surprised because I knew he was popular,” Sarah, Levi’s younger sister, added.
In the days since Levi’s death, support has been pouring in for the family.
“I just kept hearing his grandmother say, ‘Man, there’s just so many people that love Levi,’” Wetzel said. “I was like, ‘Well, he made it easy.’”
According to the Currys, two community members built a custom casket that would fit Levi’s large frame
Levi’s teammates also helped James Curry bury his son.
“The football coach, with the team, dug Levi’s grave by hand, which is something that our church does, which is very special,” James Curry said.
Nothing can ease the pain that comes with losing a child, but thanks to the support from community members, the Currys said their lives are just a little bit more peaceful.
“There’s people that we don’t even know about, that we’ve never even met, that have shown great support,” James Curry said. “For as much peace as we’ve had, we know people must be praying.”
As a family grieves, those who knew Levi are remembering his life as one filled with love.
“He knew how to lead when he needed to and he also knew when the seniors were doing their thing and leading,” Wetzel said.
Organ donation and fundraiser
According to his family, Levi was an organ donor. Hospital staff and donor recipients met to honor him this week.
A GoFundMe has been created by the family to help offset the cost of medical bills.

title: Maine men’s baskeball falls short against Drexel
text:
ORONO — Panagiotis Pagonis scored 14 points to help Drexel defeat Maine 66-64 in a men’s basketball game Saturday.
Pagonis also had seven rebounds and three steals for the Dragons (2-2). Amaree Abram shot 5 for 11, including 3 for 7 from beyond the arc, to add 13 points. Latief Lorenzano-White shot 5 for 9 and scored 11 points.
Hudson Franz led the Black Bears (1-4) with 16 points. Maine also got 15 points from Darius Lopes and 12 from Ace Flagg.
Abram scored eight points in the first half for Drexel, which led 33-30. The Dragons used a 7-0 run in the second half to build a 62-52 lead with 4:32 left, then held off a late comeback by the Black Bears.

title: Carbon monoxide toxicity suspected in death of woman, dog in mobile grooming van
text:
BEXAR COUNTY, Texas (KENS) - Two families are mourning the loss of a 10-year-old dog and the groomer who was caring for him.
The Bexar County Medical Examiner’s Office said Friday that carbon monoxide toxicity factored into the deaths.
Deputies find woman and dog unresponsive
Bexar County deputies responded Wednesday night to Dusty Boots Road after receiving a report of an injured adult. When deputies arrived, they found a woman and a dog, both unresponsive, inside a mobile grooming van.
The woman was later pronounced dead. Her identity has not been released.
The dog, Oliver, also did not survive. The dog’s owner said the family is heartbroken after losing their pet of 10 years.
“It’s just so unexpected. You’re just getting your dog groomed and then you don’t have your dog anymore,” Priscilla Coral, owner of Puptown Spa Mobile Grooming, said.
Safety questions in mobile grooming
The deaths are raising questions about safety in the mobile grooming industry.
Coral, who is not related to the deaths, operates several grooming trucks and two storefronts. She said proper ventilation, functioning carbon monoxide detectors and routine maintenance are essential to keeping both pets and workers safe.
“Having a reputable generator person, a reputable mechanic and choosing a reputable company I feel like is really important,” Coral said.
Coral said the deaths have left the mobile grooming community shaken and prompted some business owners to take a closer look at their own safety practices.
“I feel a lot of people worried, but not in a good way, but it’s brought out now people looking at safety,” Coral said.

title: 1 person trapped after vehicle lands in ditch in Orrington
text:
One person was injured Friday night when a vehicle rolled onto its side in a ditch on Snows Corner Road in Orrington.
Orrington Fire & Rescue and the Brewer Fire Department were dispatched to the area of Snows Corner and Dow roads at 7:08 p.m., according to Orrington Fire & Rescue.
Crews found one person trapped inside the vehicle. Firefighters stabilized the vehicle and freed the occupant within 18 minutes of arriving, the department said.
The person was taken to a local hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

title: 8th annual “Turkey Ride” brings Thanksgiving joy to Camden
text:
CAMDEN, Maine (WABI) - You’ve heard of a “turkey trot”: but what about a turkey ride?
Maine Sport Rockport and Camden Area Christian Food Pantry teamed up Saturday morning to give out dozens of turkeys to the local community- with an extra special twist.
Over 28 bike riders were the ones who brought donations, via their bikes!
Starting at Maine Sport Rockport, riders could take two different paths to Hannaford Supermarkets to load up on Thanksgiving favorites, then headed to Camden Area Christian Food Pantry to drop off their goods.
From their generosity, 58 families were able to receive a turkey for their Thanksgiving dinner, free of charge.
Organizers say that this unique event gives riders the opportunity to do something good for their community, all while having some turkey-themed fun.
“It’s really, really cool. Our community has supported this pantry enormously over the years. And I think for the riders to come, it just really brings them closer to what they feel is important. And it’s a fun thing to do. And it’s colorful,” said Peggy Baum, Vice President of the Camden Area Christian Food Pantry.
“If you could see them coming up the street, 30 cyclists coming up over that steep hill with turkeys on their backs,” said Debra Milliken, President of the Camden Area Christian Food Pantry.
Camden Area Christian Food Pantry updates their website and social media pages frequently with “most needed” items.
To learn more, or to donate, visit this link.

title: South Portland tank farms require strongest possible action
text:
Chelsea Byun is a South Portland resident, writer and volunteer with Protect South Portland. Lucy Perkins is a South Portland resident, community organizer and representative-elect for House District 121.
For more than 30 years, Citgo has been polluting the Pleasantdale neighborhood of South Portland, where it operates some of the 120 massive aboveground petroleum storage tanks that dominate the city’s waterfront.
We were encouraged recently when, seemingly for the first time in that history, Citgo acknowledged the harm it has caused its neighbors and the surrounding community. We urge our elected officials to act swiftly and decisively to stop that harm.
Citgo’s acknowledgement came after residents packed the lecture hall at South Portland High School to ask the City Council, at long last, to hold the city’s six tank farm operators accountable for the emissions they spew over South Portland. We now know that the air around at least five of those facilities exceeds state air quality standards for benzene, a well-studied carcinogen. This knowledge is thanks to years of advocacy by the people of South Portland who demanded better information about what living next to these tanks means for them.
The facility on Mechanic Street, operated by Citgo with a majority ownership held by Irving, was shown to be one of the worst offenders. All 18 air quality monitors placed at its fenceline consistently and often dramatically exceeded the standard for long-term benzene exposure — putting residents and employees at risk.
Homes for families, young and old, abut the facility on two sides. The city’s beloved and well-used walking and biking path passes along the fenceline. A brand new city playground, busy with children on a weekend afternoon, sits within sight of these tanks. Nine people work at the tank farm and hundreds more visit regularly, via tankers offloading fuel or trucks filling up for delivery around the state.
Oil company representatives attended the council meeting, but none spoke publicly about how they would rectify the problem. The next day, Karl Schmidt, Citgo’s vice president of marketing, sent a press release to the Press Herald and local elected officials promising quick action to reduce emissions and monitor the facility’s effects on the neighborhood. A pamphlet promoting the company’s economic impact read, in bold letters, “At Citgo, people come first.”
“We hear the community’s concerns about the study findings,” Schmidt said, “and we take those concerns seriously.” So far the company has offered no details of its emissions mitigation plan and no guarantee of cleaner air or the corporate accountability this community deserves.
City officials should not simply take Citgo at its word. Not after generations of South Portland residents have grown up with tank farms as neighbors or employers, while their worries about choking fumes, headaches, respiratory problems and the specter of long-term health risks have been dismissed and derided by oil companies and regulators alike.
In 2019, residents learned that two South Portland tank farm operators had been violating the Clean Air Act for years. The Maine Department of Environmental Protection knew this and had refused to act. Since then, city officials and community members have been asking the DEP whether the air in South Portland is safe. State regulators have said over and over that they need more data, even while they have engaged in years of testing and are, themselves, the arbiters of which data are collected. They repeated this message on Oct. 27. This time, councilors finally said, enough is enough.
“Testing in the absence of further action is not acceptable for our community,” Mayor Elyse Tipton said at the council meeting.
We agree. The City Council will hold a workshop Dec. 1 exploring its options, including a possible local ordinance, local licensing scheme or state legislation to limit emissions or require emissions controls on tank farms in South Portland.
We urge our councilors to take the strongest action they can. We need mandated emissions control, at all tank farms in South Portland. All of us — Citgo included — see the problem clearly now. It’s time to fix it.

title: FAA grounding disrupts travel for group at Bangor International Airport
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - A nationwide Federal Aviation Administration grounding on Friday canceled thousands of flights across the country, including at Bangor International Airport.
The grounding was lifted Friday evening, and planes are flying again. The cancellations have had a domino effect.
Robin Hanson drove from New Brunswick, Canada, on Friday for a morning flight Saturday.
Hanson said her group’s flight was affected by the grounding. Only two people from the eight-person group were rebooked.
Instead of splitting up, the group decided to take a bus to Boston and fly directly to Arizona from there. Hanson said the extra bus trip and stay are coming out of the group’s pockets.
“We debated on whether we should just cancel, get a full refund, and go home,” Hanson said. “But we decided, no, let’s just all decide together.”
She described the last two days as nerve-wracking.
“It’s kind of nerve-wracking,” Hanson said. “Because, I mean, was this grounding a glitch, or is there something else going on in this world? Who knows, right?”
Hanson said the national grounding will cut two days from her trip. She said she has never been to Boston.
